units.question_template: How's your energy right now compared to a typical day -- more tired than usual?
units.source_excerpt: People who are fatigued struggle to get through normal daily activities. Everyday tasks such as getting dressed can take a lot of effort, as it takes more concentration to perform tasks that are no longer automatic.

units.question_template: Is it closer to your next dose than usual right now -- does this happen more as a dose wears off?
units.source_excerpt: You are better able to move after your medications take effect, and you might find it more difficult to move as the medication wears off, before your next dose.

units.question_template: Have you been feeling anxious, worried, or on edge today?
units.source_excerpt: Anxiety can show up in different ways, such as constant worry, fear of social situations or sudden panic attacks.

units.question_template: How did you sleep last night -- any more trouble than usual falling or staying asleep?
units.source_excerpt: Sleep challenges affect more than 75% of people with PD. One difficult night can affect the next day.

units.question_template: It sounds like something may have happened that needs more than this check-in can help with. If you're injured or need help right now, please contact your doctor or local emergency services -- this system can't do that for you. Would you like to continue the check-in?
Have you noticed any new unsteadiness, trouble with balance, or near-falls recently?
units.source_excerpt: Balance issues -- PD can disrupt natural movements, posture and reflexes that help you stay steady and upright. Do you feel unsteady when walking?
units.source_version: Parkinson's Foundation, Fall Prevention in Parkinson's fact sheet

units.question_template: Where have you noticed that, and has being understood in everyday conversations changed?
units.source_excerpt: Approximately 90% of persons with Parkinson's disease (PD) experience changes in their ability to communicate ... Perhaps you have grown tired of being asked to repeat yourself in social situations and are gradually becoming more withdrawn and socially isolated.
units.source_version: APDA, Make Your Voice Heard! Healthy Communication and Parkinson's Disease, p.2

units.question_template: How often do people ask you to repeat what you said -- has that changed recently?
units.source_excerpt: Do others have trouble hearing or understanding me?
units.source_version: Parkinson's Foundation, Speech & Swallowing in Parkinson's, June 2025

units.question_template: Do you notice yourself running out of breath partway through a sentence, or needing to break sentences into shorter pieces?
units.source_excerpt: Speak in shorter phrases. When you speak in longer sentences you may notice that you start to run out of air towards the end of the sentence. This will make your voice quieter.
units.source_version: APDA, Make Your Voice Heard! Healthy Communication and Parkinson's Disease, p.9

units.question_template: Have people been asking you to speak up, or mentioning your voice sounds softer than usual?
units.source_excerpt: If you have been diagnosed with PD, you may notice that your voice is softer and breathy or hoarse, or that your speech is unclear or comes out too slowly or too fast.
units.source_version: APDA, Make Your Voice Heard! Healthy Communication and Parkinson's Disease, p.2

units.question_template: Does it feel like your speech has been coming out faster or slower than usual lately?
units.source_excerpt: Persons with PD may find themselves talking either faster or slower than usual and may notice that it can be difficult to control the speed of their speech.
units.source_version: APDA, Make Your Voice Heard! Healthy Communication and Parkinson's Disease, p.11

units.question_template: Does this tend to happen more at certain times of day, especially before your next dose of medication?
units.source_excerpt: Adjusting PD medications may also help, especially if symptoms happen during 'off' times.
units.source_version: Parkinson's Foundation, Speech & Swallowing in Parkinson's, June 2025

units.question_template: Have you noticed yourself clearing your throat more while eating or drinking, or taking longer to eat than you used to?
units.source_excerpt: Do I clear my throat often when eating or drinking? Does it take longer to eat than others?
units.source_version: Parkinson's Foundation, Speech & Swallowing in Parkinson's, June 2025

units.question_template: Was anything going on around you during that pause -- noise, a distraction, or someone interrupting?
